texts.orig: ABSTRACT
texts.text: ABSTRACT

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Hepatitis B vaccination is the most effective means of interrupting HBV transmission. Although the hepatitis B vaccine is very effective and safe, adverse events following immunization do occur and need to be reported so that problems can be identified and appropriate corrective action can be taken. Most of the research on AEFI focuses on the safety observation of newly used vaccines, and there are few long-term studies on AEFI of the hepatitis B vaccine. This study retrospectively analyzes the reporting rate, clinical symptoms, and onset time of AEFI of the hepatitis B vaccine in Quzhou from 2011 to 2023, and compares the differences in AEFI reporting rates between different types of hepatitis B vaccines, different vaccination ages, and different doses. The surveillance results show that from 2011 to 2023, the AEFI reporting rate of hepatitis B Vaccines in Quzhou was 17.55/100,000 doses. 98.73% of reported AEFI were non-serious. The types of AEFI reported were vaccine product-related reactions, immunization anxiety-related reactions, and coincidental events. 94.12% of vaccine productrelated reactions occurred within 3 days, and the main symptoms were fever, local reactions at the injection site, and rash. The AEFI reporting rate of the CHO vaccine was higher than that of the yeast vaccines, and the probability of AEFI in children under 1 year of age receiving the hepatitis B vaccine was higher in the latter dose than in the previous dose. The 13-year-long AEFI surveillance provides reliable evidence of the safety of the hepatitis B vaccine.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Hepatitis B virus (HBV), which causes both acute and chronic liver disease, is a serious global public health threat that significantly increases the global burden of disease and mortality. The World Health Organization (WHO) estimated in 2019 that 296 million people worldwide had chronic HBV infection and more than 820,000 people died prematurely from liver cancer and cirrhosis. 1 , 2 China is the country with the highest burden of HBV infection, 3 with approximately 90 million people suffering from chronic HBV infection, and approximately 300,000 people dying each year from chronic HBV infectionrelated diseases. 4 Hepatitis B vaccination is the most effective means of interrupting HBV transmission. In line with WHO recommendations, 190 countries around the world have included the hepatitis B vaccine in their national childhood immunization programs. 5 Due to the widespread use of the hepatitis B vaccine, the global prevalence of chronic HBV infection in children under 5 years of age had declined from 4.7% pre-vaccination to less than 1% in 2019. 6 Compared with the prevaccine era, chronic HBV infection in China had reduced by 90% among children <15 years of age and by 97% among children <5 years of age in 2014. 7

An unconfirmed adverse event following hepatitis B vaccination, which resulted in the suspension of safe vaccination, greatly undermining the confidence of physicians and the public in the safety of the hepatitis B vaccine. 10 , 11 Although the adverse event was eventually confirmed as a coincidence and allergy by a joint investigation by experts from the WHO and China's National AEFI Committee, the panic caused by it led to a 30% drop in the hepatitis B vaccine coverage rate in December 2013 compared with the same period in 2012, posing a threat of infection to the health of newborns. 11 Assuring the public that AEFI is under surveillance and actions are being taken to reduce the risk is critical to preventing vaccine panic and building trust. WHO recommends that all countries systematically collect, analyze, and evaluate AEFI to respond appropriately and quickly to reduce the negative impact on individual health and immunization programs. China first started conducting pilot AEFI surveillance in some provinces in 2005. 12 In June 2010, the Ministry of Health of China and the State Medical Products Administration jointly issued the Surveillance Program for Adverse Events Following Immunization in China, officially implementing AEFI surveillance nationwide. All AEFIs are reported to the surveillance system by healthcare providers, screened, and triaged by trained immunization program staff, who verify the diagnosis and timing of immunization and classify them according to standardized national case definitions. The year 2011 was the first year in which China officially launched national AEFI surveillance and carried out stan -dardized surveys and causality assessments, and since that year China's AEFI surveillance indicators have all met or exceeded WHO's assessment standards.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The AEFI data for 2011–2023 were obtained from the Chinese AEFI surveillance system, and the vaccination data were obtained from the National Immunization Program Information Management System. In cases where individuals received two or more vaccines simultaneously, we attributed the reported AEFI to the reported suspected vaccine according to the following principles: (1) Local reactions at the injection site were identified through vaccination records; (2) For systemic reactions, reported AEFIs were attributed to all vaccines administered concomitantly. Before the data were analyzed, the database was reviewed, duplicate records were eliminated, and inconsistencies were corrected.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The AEFIs are divided into five categories: (1) vaccine product-related reactions, (2) vaccine quality defect-related reactions, (3) immunization error-related reactions, (4) immunization anxiety-related reactions, and (5) coincidental events. All AEFIs are assessed as a non-serious reaction or serious reaction: (1) non-serious reaction, a situation where no intervention is necessary or there is a physician visit or an event that interferes with daily activities or results in loss of working hours, (2) serious reaction, a situation with any untoward medical occurrence that results in death, hospitalization, prolongation of hospitalization, persistent or significant disability/incapacity, and life-threatening conditions or birth defects.

texts.text: Discussion

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Conducting standardized AEFI investigations and causal relationship assessments and maintaining the surveillance capacity and sensitivity for AEFI of the hepatitis B vaccine will help enhance public confidence in hepatitis B immunization. The 13-year AEFI surveillance of the hepatitis B vaccine in Quzhou showed that adverse events were usually mild and transient, non-serious, such as fever, local injection site reactions, and rash. Records of serious reactions were extremely rare. The AEFI surveillance of the hepatitis B vaccine in Quzhou provides reliable evidence for the safety of the hepatitis B vaccine in China.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Data from the AEFI Surveillance System indicate that the reported rate of AEFIs of hepatitis B vaccine in Quzhou from 2011–2023 was 17.55/100,000 doses. The reported rate of AEFIs of hepatitis B vaccine in Guangdong Province was 3.54/100,000 from 2005 to 2017, 17 and the reported rate of AEFIs of hepatitis B vaccine in China was 14.8/100,000 doses in 2020. 18 The sensitivity of AEFI surveillance of the hepatitis B vaccine in Quzhou is higher than the national average. Compared with the reporting rate of AEFIs of hepatitis B vaccine of 11.8/100,000 doses in the United States from 1991 to 2001 and 10 .4/100,000 doses in Australia from January 1, 2000, to September 30, 2002, the reporting rate of AEFIs of the hepatitis B vaccine in Quzhou was higher. As a result of the hepatitis B vaccine safety incident in November 2013, public sensitivity to hepatitis B vaccine safety increased, and AEFIs of hepatitis B vaccine reporting rate (20.38 per 100,000 doses) in 2014 saw a small spike. From 2020 to 2022, Quzhou experienced a three-year lockdown due to COVID-19. During this period, the dose of hepatitis B vaccination decreased, and the reporting rate of AEFIs of the hepatitis B vaccine fluctuated within a small range. In 2023, after the lockdown was lifted, the hepatitis B vaccination dose increased slightly, and AEFIs of the hepatitis B vaccine reporting rate (30.73/100,000 doses) reached the highest. Overall, there was an increasing trend in the reporting of AEFIs of hepatitis B vaccine over the 13 years. This may be related to the increasing public awareness of vaccine safety and the increased sensitivity of surveillance systems. 17

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Surveillance data over 13 years showed that the vast majority of AEFIs of hepatitis B vaccine were non-serious. Two cases of serious AEFI were reported, one of which was a relatively rare thrombocytopenic purpura. Thrombocytopenic purpura is usually caused by antibodies against the platelet glycoprotein IIb/IIIa complex 19 and can be triggered by drugs, infections, cancer, and autoimmune diseases, with one of the rare triggers being vaccination. 20 This case of AEFI was found to have petechiae and ecchymosis 8 days after vaccination and recovered several days later. Another case of serious AEFI was a post-vaccination death, which was later confirmed to be an unfortunate coincidental event. texts.orig: The main symptoms of AEFIs for vaccine product-related reactions were fever, redness and swelling, rash, and induration. Fever is the most commonly reported vaccine productrelated adverse reaction following hepatitis B vaccination. This is part of the body's immune response, a useful mechanism that promotes cell, blood vessel, and metabolic defense mobilization, kills viruses, and activates immunity, but it turns into a "disease" above a certain temperature. 23 Because the aluminum adjuvants in the hepatitis B vaccines can increase local inflammatory responses and immune system responses, 24 redness swelling, and induration at the recipient's injection site are also common. But it may also have to do with the method of administration. The hepatitis B vaccine is not fully shaken before injection, and the large particles contained in the vaccine are slowly absorbed, leading to a local reaction. In addition, shorter needles or shallow injections increase the risk of vaccine-related local reactions. It is recommended to strengthen the training of vaccinators, standardize the operation of vaccination, and reduce the occurrence of local reac -tions. Rashes, including urticaria, measles scarlatina-like rash, and maculopapular, are also more commonly reported and are usually mild and do not require special treatment.

texts.orig: In terms of the time interval between vaccination and the occurrence of vaccine product-related reactions, the vast majority of reactions occurred within 3 days. This suggests that parents need to be reminded to observe children's reactions within 3 days after vaccination. The time of reaction following vaccine co-administration was faster, and the proportion of reactions occurring within 24 hours and 3 days was relatively higher than that of single. Because we could not distinguish between completed doses of hepatitis B single or co-administration, we were unable to compare the difference in AEFI reporting rates between the two. However, most studies found no statistically significant differences in the reporting rates of any AEFI following vaccine single and coadministration. 25 Vaccine co-administration is an effective vaccination strategy associated with high coverage and vaccine timeliness. 26 All recommended pediatric routine immunizations can be co-administered, and there is no recommendation against co-administration unless reported in the summary of product characteristics. Childhood vaccine co-administration is an effective strategy to maintain or even increase vaccination rates. 27

texts.orig: The yeast vaccine is a vaccine produced using yeast cells, while The CHO vaccine is a vaccine produced using hamster ovary cells. Both of them are recombinant genetically engineered vaccines, the difference mainly lies in the difference in the recombinant cell material. The reporting rate of the CHO vaccine product-related reactions was higher than that of the yeast vaccines, and the difference was statistically significant. This may be related to the higher specifications and dosage of CHO vaccines. The commonly used clinical specifications for yeast vaccines are generally 10 μg/0.5 mL/ vial, while the commonly used clinical specifications for CHO cells are generally 20 μg/1 mL/vial. In an open-label randomized trial in China, the AEFI reporting rate was comparable between 20 μg of yeast hepatitis B vaccine and 20 μg CHO hepatitis B vaccine. 29

texts.orig: The reporting rates of vaccine product-related reactions following hepatitis B vaccination vary among people of different ages. Reported rates of vaccine product-related reactions following hepatitis B vaccination were slightly higher in people aged 1 year and above than in children younger than 1 year of age, but the difference was not statistically significant. There is a high probability that people aged 1 year and above are booster-vaccinated or are in the older age group that did not receive the hepatitis B vaccine in infancy. Recipients of booster doses of hepatitis B vaccine receive repeated stimulation at the injection site, resulting in increased sensitivity to vaccine antigens or adjuvants. And older people who get vaccinated tend to be more responsive to the vaccine and more observant.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The standardized surveillance of AEFI in Quzhou has spanned 13 years, and we searched all reports of AEFIs following hepatitis B vaccination during this period, allowing for a comprehensive assessment. High-quality and sensitive AEFI records improve the reliability of surveillance analysis and provide a tool for evaluating the safety of the hepatitis B vaccine. Our description and analysis of AEFI further confirm the safety of the hepatitis B vaccine. This is important for increasing public confidence in hepatitis B vaccination and promoting adherence to the vaccination program. We found that more than 90% of AEFI occurred within three days following vaccination, especially for co-administration, the proportion of AEFI occurring within three days was even higher; the AEFI reporting rate following the third dose was significantly higher than that of the first and second doses. The surveillance results are a good reminder that we need to do a good job of observation and emergency management based on these characteristics in practice. We also found that the 20 μg CHO hepatitis B vaccine had a higher AEFI reporting rate than the 10 μg yeast hepatitis B vaccine; people over 1 year old had a higher AEFI reporting rate of hepatitis B vaccine than those under 1 year old. Our study has guiding significance for the selection of the hepatitis B vaccine in the future. When vaccinating against hepatitis B, it would be a better choice to complete the vaccination of 10 μg yeast hepatitis B vaccine within 1 year of age.

texts.orig: Active surveillance in China is still at an initial exploratory stage, with no effective active surveillance mechanism covering the whole country, and a further lack of application of advanced methods and technologies for active surveillance. Compared to the accurate and huge cost of active surveillance, passive surveillance provides extensive and economical coverage. Our data came from passive surveillance. Although it has limitations such as underreporting, late reporting, and difficulty in conducting causal analysis, it is still the most feasible method for AEFI surveillance in China. 18 Another limitation of this study is that our data were collected from Quzhou and cannot represent the whole of China.
